found_values.value: 0.129 degree or finer over 180 degrees of horn travel (+/-90). The servo screen maps the horn's full travel of 180 degrees onto the servo type's pulse span (us_to_deg: deg = (us - centre - trim) x 90 / (span / 2)) and takes the measured position as a whole number of microseconds (servo_screen_feedback(uint16_t position_us, ...)). One microsecond is 180 / 1000 = 0.18 degree on STANDARD (1000 to 2000 us), 180 / 1400 = 0.129 degree on WIDE (800 to 2200 us) and 0.9 degree on NARROW 760 (660 to 860 us); the sensor resolves the finest, 0.129 degree, so the link's 1 us step is the limit

report.value: No accelerometer shows the 1.244 us share at 1,092 Hz. ADXL316 and ADXL326 require CX of 4.7 nF or more ('Capacitors must be added', 'A minimum capacitance of 0.0047 uF ... is recommended in all cases'); with RFILT 27 to 37 kOhm (ADXL316) or 32 kOhm +/-15 % (ADXL326) the pole's delay at 1,092 Hz spans 104.40 to 127.26 us, a variation of 22.86 us (ADXL316), and 21.94 us (ADXL326). FU-2C's 1.000 us used CX = 100 pF, below that minimum; there the 1,600 Hz 'no external filter' bandwidth (typical only) governs: 87.3 us of delay at 1,092 Hz for a single pole, 0.042 us per Hz of pole movement, so the share allows 29 Hz (1.8 %), which nothing states. docs/Balance.md:65-66 says a constant delay cancels because the trial run measures the whole chain, so the spread between units would cancel; the drift of RFILT, CX and the internal response within one unit between runs is not stated for any part read. The accelerometer keeps no part. The owner decides whether the share is judged on the unit-to-unit spread (fails by 18 x), on the drift within one unit (not stated), or on a measurement

At the IO board end the ADCS7476's 26 pF sampling capacitor and 400 ns track time need a series resistor and a reservoir capacitor, stage 2 passives whose RC adds its own delay variation: for example 49.9 Ohm +/-1 % and 2.2 nF C0G +/-5 % give 110 ns +/-6.6 ns. The edge a pen line gives is also set by the spot size and the bell's surface speed: 1 mm crossing a 28 mm bell at 65,535 rpm takes about 10 us, so a change in reflected amplitude moves the threshold crossing inside that edge by a fraction of it, which no part figure bounds (a bell diameter of 28 mm and a 1 mm spot are assumptions).
